description: On November 4, 2020, the TPLF launched an attack on the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defense Force in Tigray. Prime Minister Abiy responded with a military offensive to dislodge the TPLF from power in the region.

title: COVID-19 pandemic response in Ethiopia
description: Ethiopia confirmed its first COVID-19 case in March 2020 and imposed public health measures including school closures and curfews. The pandemic compounded existing humanitarian challenges from ethnic violence and the early stages of the Tigray conflict.

title: Ethiopia wins bid to host African Continental Free Trade Secretariat
description: Addis Ababa was selected as the headquarters for the African Continental Free Trade Area secretariat, reinforcing its status as Africa's institutional capital. The selection reflected Ethiopia's diplomatic weight and existing AU infrastructure.

title: TPLF launches massive counteroffensive, recaptures Tigray
description: In June 2021, the TPLF launched a major counteroffensive that routed federal and Eritrean forces, recapturing most of Tigray. The TPLF then advanced into Afar and Amhara regions, bringing the war to new territories.

title: Humanitarian catastrophe in Tigray: famine conditions declared
description: International agencies declared famine conditions in parts of Tigray in 2021, with estimates of 400,000 people in famine. Deliberate blockage of aid access, destruction of infrastructure, and mass displacement drove the catastrophe.

title: Ethiopia suspends US aid and expels UN officials
description: The Ethiopian government expelled several senior UN officials it accused of interference in internal affairs and suspended US aid programs after Washington imposed sanctions. The confrontation marked a major deterioration in Ethiopia-US relations.

title: Axum atrocity: hundreds killed in historical city
description: Ethiopian and Eritrean forces killed hundreds of civilians in the ancient holy city of Axum in November 2020, in what human rights organizations described as a massacre. The killings at one of Christianity's most sacred African sites drew particular international condemnation.

title: Tigray ceasefire agreement signed in Pretoria
description: The Ethiopian government and TPLF signed a Cessation of Hostilities Agreement in Pretoria, South Africa on November 2, 2022, ending two years of devastating conflict. The agreement provided for disarmament of TPLF forces and restoration of federal administration in Tigray.

title: TPLF advances to within 200 km of Addis Ababa before reversal
description: TPLF forces advanced into Amhara and Afar regions in late 2021 and early 2022, threatening Addis Ababa and triggering mass military mobilization. A federal counteroffensive in late 2022 reversed TPLF gains before the Pretoria ceasefire.

title: Tigray War death toll estimated at 300,000-500,000
description: Studies published in 2022 estimated the Tigray War had killed between 300,000 and 500,000 people through combat, famine, and disease. The conflict became one of the deadliest wars of the 21st century.

title: Ethiopia joins African Continental Free Trade Area
description: Ethiopia ratified and began implementing the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement, seeking to expand export markets. The government prioritized export-oriented manufacturing, particularly textiles and garments, as a source of foreign exchange.

title: Ethiopia receives $300 million World Bank emergency support
description: The World Bank approved emergency financing for Ethiopia to address humanitarian needs related to the Tigray conflict, drought, and economic stress. The support came with conditions tied to governance and conflict resolution.

title: Tigray peace implementation begins but stalls
description: Implementation of the Pretoria peace agreement began with TPLF disarmament and restoration of humanitarian access to Tigray. However, key provisions including withdrawal of Eritrean forces and territorial disputes with Amhara remained unresolved.

title: Amhara region conflict escalates: Fano militias confront federal forces
description: Armed conflict broke out in Amhara region between federal forces and Fano militia groups that had fought alongside the government in Tigray. The conflict reflected Amhara grievances over federal governance and loss of Wolkait territory.

title: Ethiopia defaults on Eurobond, seeks debt restructuring
description: Ethiopia defaulted on its Eurobond debt in December 2023, becoming one of several African countries seeking debt restructuring under the G20 Common Framework. The default reflected fiscal pressures from war, drought, and global interest rate increases.

title: Tigray famine conditions persist despite ceasefire
description: Despite the November 2022 ceasefire, famine conditions persisted in parts of Tigray due to damaged infrastructure, depleted household assets, and slow aid delivery. The humanitarian crisis remained among the world's most severe.

title: Ethiopia launches new telecom operator, ending monopoly
description: Safaricom Ethiopia launched commercial services, ending Ethio Telecom's monopoly and bringing mobile money services to Ethiopia for the first time. The telecom liberalization was one of the most significant economic reforms of the Abiy era.

title: Ethiopia signs memorandum with Somaliland for sea access
description: Ethiopia signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland providing access to the Red Sea coast in exchange for recognition and potential equity in Ethiopian Airlines. The deal triggered intense diplomatic protests from Somalia and raised regional tensions.

title: Conflict in Amhara region continues with no resolution
description: Fighting between Ethiopian federal forces and Fano militia groups continued throughout 2024, causing widespread displacement and humanitarian needs in Amhara. The conflict undermined Ethiopia's post-Tigray stabilization narrative.

title: Ethiopia joins BRICS as full member
description: Ethiopia formally became a BRICS member in January 2024 alongside four other countries, completing its application from the previous year. The membership reflected Ethiopia's ambitions to assert itself as a major African economic and diplomatic power.

title: Tigray reconstruction begins amid continued Eritrean presence
description: Reconstruction efforts began in war-devastated Tigray, but Eritrean troops remained in parts of the region despite the Pretoria agreement's requirements. The continued Eritrean presence remained a major obstacle to full implementation of the peace deal.

title: Ethiopia's population reaches 130 million
description: Ethiopia's population grew to an estimated 130 million, making it Africa's second most populous country after Nigeria. Rapid population growth continued to challenge the government's efforts to improve living standards and employment opportunities.

title: GERD begins commercial power generation
description: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam began commercial electricity generation at increased capacity, fulfilling a core ambition of Ethiopian energy policy. The dam's output began addressing Ethiopia's severe power deficit and created export potential.

title: Oromia security crisis: OLA confrontations with federal forces
description: The Oromo Liberation Army continued confrontations with Ethiopian security forces in western and southern Oromia, causing significant civilian displacement. Peace talks between the OLA and federal government remained inconclusive.

title: Lethal floods hit Gambella and SNNP regions
description: Severe flooding in Gambella and Southern Nations regions killed hundreds of people and displaced over half a million during the 2024 rainy season. The disasters reflected worsening climate impacts on Ethiopia's vulnerability to extreme weather.
